Audit EVERY LINE of the admin portal of the Nxeon VPS hosting platform at /opt/nxeon. This is the operations console for a real hosting business: it can suspend customers, refund money, impersonate accounts and destroy servers. A prior attempt was killed by a session limit; start fresh from the clean committed tree.

YOUR FILES (owned exclusively): everything under `app/admin/**` and `components/admin/**`. NOT yours (read, change only if NEW): lib/rbac.ts (audited this session), components/admin/ServerAdminActions.tsx (just changed this session — read but do not re-edit unless you find something new).

READ EVERY LINE. Enumerate every admin page and component first and account for all of them.

WHAT MATTERS MOST, in order:
1. **Authorisation that exists only in the UI.** An admin page hiding a control from a role, while the underlying server action does not check that role, is not a permission — it is decoration. For every control, find the action behind it and verify the role check lives INSIDE the action. RBAC areas are in `lib/rbac.ts` (`canAccess`/`requireArea`); check each admin surface enforces its area server-side, not by not rendering a link. Note: this session established that every export of a "use server" file is a network-callable endpoint — enumerate the exports behind admin pages and confirm each is guarded inside the function.
2. **Impersonation.** An admin acting as a customer must never SPEND that customer's money — there is an `assertNotImpersonating` guard, and this session found and fixed seven money paths missing it. Verify every admin-initiated action touching a customer's balance, and that the impersonation banner cannot be lost (session and impersonation cookies were interchangeable until this session; both are now typed with a `typ` claim — verify admin flows rely on that).
3. **Destructive controls without proportionate friction.** Suspend, terminate, delete server, delete backup, force-refund. Does the confirmation state the REAL consequence — that terminating destroys the VM AND the customer's separately-billed volumes? Does anything destructive lack a confirmation entirely?
4. **Numbers that are wrong or unverified.** MRR, capacity, server counts, revenue, "all systems operational". Check each figure is computed from what it claims to measure. This platform has repeatedly shipped a surface reporting an outcome it never verified (a migration scoring 4/4 with six domains dark; a backup timestamp written at enqueue). Look for admin figures with the same shape, and any hardcoded status indicator.
5. **Audit trail integrity.** `audit()` attributes actions to the real admin when impersonating. Verify every consequential admin action writes an audit row recording WHO actually did it.

DESIGN: match the existing admin design system exactly — read neighbouring pages, reuse their tokens and vocabulary. The owner has been explicit everything must match the Nxeon theme.

VERIFY, reporting only what you observed:
- `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit ; echo "exit=$?"` — must be 0.
- `cd /opt/nxeon && npm test` — currently 541 passing; must stay green and grow.
- Exercise against STAGING (`nxeon-staging-web`, port 3001) where you can; say plainly which findings you RAN versus only READ.
- Do NOT run `npm run build` in place — production is served from /opt/nxeon/.next.
- For every fix add a test and PROVE it bites by reverting it. Tripwires MUST use `stripCommentsAndStrings` from `test/_source-tools.ts` — a naive grep matches this repo's own incident notes and passes on broken code.

HAZARDS: never suspend, terminate, refund, impersonate or delete anything belonging to a real account — there is one real customer VM (`soulpilates`) and real users in the production database. Do NOT run standalone scripts from a tree with symlinked node_modules — Prisma loads production's DATABASE_URL; an agent seeded the production database that way this week. Do not deploy, restart production services, or commit.

Report: the full admin page inventory with a verdict each, then every defect with file:line and what it would let an operator (or a lower-privileged staff member) do, what you fixed, which tripwires you proved, RAN vs READ, and what you could not verify.

My audit is complete. Here is the full report.

## Scope & method
I read the security spine first (`lib/auth.ts`, `lib/rbac.ts`, `audit()`, `admin-metrics.ts`), built a static guard-map of every `"use server"` export, personally read the crown-jewel surfaces (layout, users/[id], all admin money/lifecycle actions, serverAction/ownedServer + the worker delete path), and fanned the remaining ~40 pages/components to four parallel readers whose findings I then verified first-hand before acting. **RAN:** `tsc --noEmit` (exit 0), the full `npm test` (**582 pass / 0 fail**, up from 541), and every new tripwire proven to bite by revert-then-restore. **READ-only (could not RAN):** the authenticated admin pages against staging — they are host/IP/2FA/login-gated so an unauthenticated curl never executes the page code, and standalone Prisma scripts are forbidden (production `DATABASE_URL` hazard). Type-checking + the test suite are my execution evidence.

## The headline finding
`lib/admin-metrics.ts` was written (with past-tense docstrings claiming `/admin`, `/admin/subscriptions`, `/admin/analytics` were all fixed) and wired into the **overview only**. **billing, subscriptions, and analytics still carried the exact buggy math the helpers exist to kill** — the prior session died mid-migration. The promised test (`test/admin-console-guards.test.ts`) was never written either. A refund made "Revenue" go **up**; game servers and long-term/suspended servers mis-priced MRR.

## Admin page inventory (verdict each)
**Overview/finance:** overview CLEAN · analytics **FIXED** · billing **FIXED** · subscriptions **FIXED** · invoices CLEAN · invoices/[id] **FIXED** (money-form confirm) · plans/coupons/game-plans/email-plans/products CLEAN · gift-codes **FIXED** · affiliate **FIXED** (+reported)
**Fleet:** servers REPORTED · servers/[id] **FIXED** (+reported) · nodes,nodes/[id],nodes/new CLEAN · ips REPORTED · provisioning/jobs/monitoring CLEAN · infrastructure REPORTED · abuse **FIXED**
**Clients/support/content:** users, users/[id] CLEAN (exemplary) · orgs CLEAN · support, support/[id] CLEAN · feedback CLEAN (minor reported) · chat **FIXED** · testimonials/blog/newsletter REPORTED · games/email-templates CLEAN
**Platform:** automation **FIXED** · visitors/audit/logs/mail/domains/grant/staff/improvements/docs CLEAN · settings CLEAN (+reported) · layout/error/loading CLEAN

Layout defenses verified: admin-host gate → 404, staff-only, impersonation-exit redirect, IP allow-list (fails open safely), staff-2FA enforcement, role-filtered nav.

## Defects I fixed (file:line · impact · fix · tripwire)
1. **Revenue counts refunds as revenue** — `app/admin/billing/page.tsx:20-28`, `subscriptions/page.tsx:18`, `analytics/page.tsx:24,44`. A `SUM(amountCents<0)` counted refunds, affiliate cash-outs and admin debits as revenue. Fixed to `REVENUE_WHERE`. Tripwire: *"every page that shows revenue derives it from REVENUE_WHERE"*.
2. **MRR priced at base VPS rate** — `subscriptions/page.tsx:25` (`sum + plan.priceCents`), `analytics/page.tsx:94`. Ignored game-plan flat pricing, term proration, and suspended-server exclusion. Fixed to `fleetMrrCents`/`serverMonthlyCents` (added `gamePlan` includes). Tripwire: *"every page that shows MRR derives it from serverMonthlyCents/fleetMrrCents"* + unit tests for game/term/suspended.
3. **"Credits issued" missed the page's own tool** — `billing/page.tsx:29`. Matched only `"Admin credit"`, invisible to `adjustBalance` ("Admin balance adjustment"). Fixed to `ADMIN_CREDIT_WHERE`.
4. **Hardcoded "online" status dots** — `app/admin/automation/page.tsx:52,82,108,132`, under a "no vapourware" banner. All-green even with `nxeon-worker` dead. Fixed: three worker dots driven by real `workerHealth()`, improvement-agent dot from ROADMAP.md mtime. Tripwire: *"automation page derives every status dot from a real signal"*.
5. **Delete confirmation omitted separately-billed volumes** — `components/admin/ServerAdminActions.tsx:66` + `app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx:288`. DELETE runs `qm destroy --purge` and the worker deletes every Volume row (worker/index.ts `remove`), yet the confirm said only "VM, disk, IP, port forwards". Fixed both copies to name attached data volumes. (This is the new finding justifying the ServerAdminActions edit.) Tripwires: 2, both proven.
6. **One-click money movers** — `components/admin/RefundControls.tsx`. Refund-to-card and negative wallet debit fired with no confirmation while neighbours confirm. Added `onSubmit` confirm+`preventDefault`. Tripwire: *"both admin money forms confirm before moving money"*.
7. **Capped-list totals under-report** — `chat/page.tsx` (take:200), `gift-codes/page.tsx` (take:500), `affiliate/page.tsx` (take:500) derived headline totals/liability from the display page. Fixed to DB `count()`/`aggregate()`. Tripwire proven.
8. **Abuse queue writes unattributed** — `lib/actions-abuse.ts` `acknowledgeAlert`/`resolveAlert` closed cases with no audit row (sibling `suspendForAbuse` logged). Added `auditLog` rows. Tripwire: *"every abuse-queue write records who did it"*.

Plus a **new structural net** (`test/admin-actions-guards.test.ts`): enumerates all 17 admin/staff action modules and proves every export both authenticates *and* reaches for STAFF authority (not bare `requireUser`) — the coverage `customer-actions-guards.test.ts` never extended to admin. Proven to bite when a `requireAdmin` is downgraded to `requireUser`.

## Authorization: verified clean, no new hole
Every admin control's backing action enforces its role **inside** the function (`requireAdmin`/`requireArea`/`ownedServer`), not in the UI — users/[id] even documents the "UI removes what the action refuses" principle. Impersonation objective (#2): layout redirects impersonators out, `typ`-claim separation is intact, `audit()` re-attributes to the real admin — no new money path missing the guard.

## Reported, not fixed (with reasons)
- **Suspend one-click, no confirm** — `components/AdminControls.tsx:17,24` (`SuspendServerButton`/`SuspendUserButton`). Real friction gap, but **outside my owned tree** (a concurrent agent is editing customer/portal); left untouched to avoid collision.
- **Infrastructure capacity hardcoded** — `app/admin/infrastructure/page.tsx:206` (`ipCount`, fleet-wide, shown against a hardcoded single-/24 `150` on a multi-node platform), `:201` fixed subnet, `:74` silent 64 GB RAM fallback driving the capacity ratio. Needs a per-node subnet model; deferred rather than guess.
- **Content-op audit gaps** — `actions-blog.ts`, `actions-testimonials.ts`, `actions-newsletter-campaign.ts` (delete/publish/`sendCampaign` to all subscribers), `actions-feedback.ts:adminUpdateFeedback`, `actions-ovh.ts` (`syncIpPool`/`releaseIpFromServer`/`setIpReverse`) write no `auditLog`. `sendCampaign` (mass email, unattributed) is the most notable.
- **Settings guard weaker than page area** — `lib/actions-settings.ts:196` `BILLING_SECTIONS` lets a BILLING staffer POST `dunning_terminate_days` (the day a VM is destroyed) though the page is ADMIN-only. Documented as intentional and range-validated — flag for owner to confirm the trust boundary.
- **Defense-in-depth**: `refundPayment`/`adjustBalance`/`adminUpdatePayout` lack `assertNotImpersonating` (mitigated today by the layout impersonation-exit redirect).

## Couldn't verify
The authenticated admin pages rendering against live staging (auth/host/IP-gated; standalone Prisma forbidden). `ServerConsole` VNC authorization lives in an API route, not an action — outside this pass; worth a separate check that it gates admins/owners server-side. Nothing was committed, deployed, or run against real accounts.
